Research Theme: Theme 1: Decisions on governance mode and mechanism
Context: In the context of high asset specificity, volume uncertainty, and behavioral uncertainty
Intervention: choosing hierarchical governance
Outcome: leads to enhanced performance (Geyskens et al., 2006).

Research Theme: Theme 1: Decisions on governance mode and mechanism
Context: In the context of low asset specificity, volume uncertainty, and behavioral uncertainty
Intervention: choosing market governance
Outcome: leads to enhanced performance (Geyskens et al., 2006).

Research Theme: Theme 1: Decisions on governance mode and mechanism
Context: In the context of make-or-buy decisions
Intervention: maintaining some knowledge of the outsourced activity/technology
Outcome: increases outsourcing benefits (Tiwana and Keil, 2007; Bustinza et al., 2010; Handley, 2012).

Research Theme: Theme 1: Decisions on governance mode and mechanism
Context: In the context of alliances with property based assets (Poppo and Zenger, 2002) and innovative, short life-cycle products with significant business uncertainties(Mahapatra et al., 2010), volatility (Carson et al., 2006)
Intervention: emphasizing formal contracts as governance mechanism
Outcome: safeguards opportunism (Poppo and Zenger, 2002; Carson et al., 2006; Mahapatra et al., 2012).

Research Theme: Theme 1: Decisions on governance mode and mechanism
Context: In the context of alliances with knowledge based assets(Poppo and Zenger, 2002), and ambiguity (Carson et al.,2006)
Intervention: emphasizing relational contracts as the governance mechanism
Outcome: reduces opportunism (Poppo and Zenger, 2002; Carson et al.,2006).

Research Theme: Theme 2: Network formation and relationship initiation
Context: In the context of network formation
Intervention: building strong relational ties with trustworthy partners
Outcome: supports exploitation activities to improve firm effectivenessand performance (Beverland, 2005; Tiwana, 2008; Rowley et al., 2000).

Research Theme: Theme 2: Network formation and relationship initiation
Context: In the context of network formation
Intervention: building a great number of versatile weak ties
Outcome: supports exploration activities to develop innovations and improve firm performance (Beverland, 2005; Tiwana, 2008; Rowley et al., 2000).

Research Theme: Theme 2: Network formation and relationship initiation
Context: In the context of network formation
Intervention: maintaining a rich portfolio of bridging ties to network resources
Outcome: supports firm's innovations through access to new ideas,information and opportunities (McEvily and Zaheer, 1999;Tiwana, 2008; Choi and Kim, 2008).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: increasing interfirm trust, commitment and/or using relational norms
Outcome: mproves relationship performance (Laaksonen et al., 2008;Whipple and Frankel, 2000; Johnston et al., 2004; Nyaga et al.,2010; Krishnan et al., 2006), including financial and relational outcomes (Palmatier et al., 2007);improves shared planning and flexibility in arrangements(Johnston et al., 2004);improves satisfaction (Nyaga et al., 2010);increases relationship effectiveness (Smith, 1997).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: collaboration/co-operation/transformational leadership in relationships
Outcome: leads to higher satisfaction with the relationship, satisfaction with performance and a higher performance (Whipple et al.,2010);increases relationship commitment (Hult et al., 2000);delivers positive supply chain operational and financial performance benefits (Fawcett et al., 2012).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: adaptive behavior within a relationship
Outcome: increases levels of trust and enhance commitment (Brennan and Turnbull, 1999);improves quality of produced products (Hagberg-Andersson,2006).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: use of noncoercive influence strategies (Rationality, Recommendations, Information Exchange, and Requests)
Outcome: increases compliance by the target firm (Payan and McFarland,2005);increases trust, commitment, and joint action (Hausman and Johnston, 2010);improves supplier's delivery flexibility under high shared vision (Chang and Huang, 2012);leads to lower conflict (Leonidou et al., 2008).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: accumulating relational capital
Outcome: increases the (operational and strategic) performance in the relationship (Kohtam?ki et al., 2012; Cousins et al., 2006; Villena et al., 2011);supports the growth of a SME by enhancing the transition between different growth phases (Partanen et al., 2008).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: shaping customer attraction and increasing supplier satisfaction
Outcome: increases preferential treatment by suppliers. (Huttinger et al.,2012; Baxter, 2012) and makes a supplier voluntarily develop the relationship (Hald et al., 2009).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: using socialization as a tactic in influencing
Outcome: increases supply chain relational capital (Cousins et al., 2006);improves communication between the companies (van de Vijver and Akkermans, 2011; Cousins and Menguc, 2006);increases operational performance (Cousins and Menguc,2006).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: adopting procedural,distributive and interactional justice policies
Outcome: increases alliance performance (Liu et al., 2012) measured as asset turnover (Luo, 2007);decreases conflict and increase satisfaction and influence the distributer's performance (Griffith et al., 2006).

Research Theme: Theme 3: Interorganizational relationships
Context: In both supplier and customer relationships
Intervention: increasing (perceived) dependency
Outcome: increases relationship effectiveness (Smith, 1997);supports the development of relational capital (Petersen et al.,2008);increases the commitment of the parties (Goodman and Dion, 2001) and influences customer attraction (Hald et al., 2009).

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In strategic alliances (dyadic context)
Intervention: experiences and learning from alliances
Outcome: promote alliance success (Kale et al., 2002);increase alliance benefits (Chen et al., 2004; Prahinski and Benton, 2004; Sampson, 2005)

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In strategic alliances (dyadic context)
Intervention: investment in alliance learning tools
Outcome: increases alliance capability (Sluyts et al., 2011).

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In strategic alliances (dyadic context)
Intervention: supplier development activities
Outcome: increase supplier performance (Krause, 1997; Morris and Carter, 2016; Das et al., 2006; Lai, 2007; Modi and Mabert,2007);lower supplier costs (Rogers et al., 2007).

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In strategic alliances (dyadic context)
Intervention: partner complementarities
Outcome: improve alliance performance (Rothaermel, 2001; Tiwana and Keil, 2007).

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In supply networks (network context)
Intervention: co-operative relationships between suppliers
Outcome: negatively influence supplier performance (Saxton, 1997; Wu et al., 2010).

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In supply networks (network context)
Intervention: integration with suppliers and customers
Outcome: increases supply performance (Frohlich and Westbrook, 2001);improves time-based performance and overall firm performance (Stock et al., 2000; Malhotra and Mackelprang,2012).

Research Theme: Theme 4: Strategic aspects of exploiting external resources
Context: In supply networks (network context)
Intervention: integrated information technologies and information sharing
Outcome: increase supply performance (Vickery et al., 2003; Dyer and Hatch, 2006).

Research Theme: Theme 5: Open innovation and interorganizational learning
Context: In the context of new product development
Intervention: involving customers in the NPD project
Outcome: increase the likelihood of successful major innovations(Coviello and Joseph, 2012).fasten the speed to markets (Fang, 2008);improve product quality, delivery, and reliability (Feng et al.,2010);improves market and project performance (Mishra and Shah,2009);improves customer satisfaction (Tan and Tracey, 2007);Improves manufacturing agility (Tracey, 2004).

Research Theme: Theme 5: Open innovation and interorganizational learning
Context: In the context of new product development
Intervention: involving suppliers in the NPD project
Outcome: decreases costs (Feng et al., 2010);reduces delays (Hartley et al., 1997);increases product innovation (only grey box) (Koufteros et al.,2007);improves project and market performance (Mishra and Shah,2009);improves financial results and product design performance(Petersen et al., 2005);improves product quality (Primo and Amundson, 2002);improves manufacturing performance (Vonderembse and Tracey, 1999);improves customer satisfaction (Tan and Tracey, 2007);improves manufacturing agility (Tracey, 2004).

Research Theme: Theme 5: Open innovation and interorganizational learning
Context: In the context of new product development
Intervention: investing in technologically diverse alliances
Outcome: increases firm's innovations (Lundberg and Andresen, 2012);predicts products on markets (Rothaermel and Deeds, 2004).

Research Theme: Theme 6: Operational practices of managing external resources
Context: In supplier relationships
Intervention: the use of e-business technologies such as EDI
Outcome: increases supplier reliability and lowers acquisition cost(Walton and Marucheck, 1997);improves organizational performance (Feng et al., 2012);decreases relationship conflict (Yan and Wang, 2012);improves organizational performance (Feng et al., 2012).

Research Theme: Theme 6: Operational practices of managing external resources
Context: In supplier relationships
Intervention: a right level of internal and external integration
Outcome: improves operational performance (Stump and Sriram, 1997;Li et al., 2005; Li et al., 2010);improves lead-time performance (Stock et al., 2000; Garver,2003);increases supplier reliability and lowers acquisition costs(Malhotra and Mackelprang, 2012);positively impacts a firm's supply chain agility (L?sch and Lambert, 2007).

Research Theme: Theme 6: Operational practices of managing external resources
Context: In supplier relationships
Intervention: good communication and information sharing
Outcome: lower operation costs (face-to-face and written/electronic) and acquisition costs (written/electronic only) (Pearcy et al.,2007);improve lead-time performance (Malhotra and Mackelprang,2012);improve suppliers' compliance to buyer's code of conduct(Cannon and Homburg, 2001);improve supplier's performance (Sanders, 2007).
